Scenarios.Scenario: Load the AI customization fixture module and mount the folder's themed screenshot fixtures
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Module evaluation registers one lightweight Extensions contribution in an in-memory Map before fixtures render. This replaces render-time registration in two fixtures and adds no asynchronous prerequisite, filesystem, network, IPC, subprocess, or database work.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One fixture module load and one registry contribution, independent of fixture count and theme variants; the contribution stores constant metadata and function references.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The module-level registration occurs synchronously once per module instance. Fixture renders may coexist, but they only read the shared contribution and do not schedule concurrent expensive work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The registry Map is the shared lookup structure; the contribution is retained for the module lifetime. There are no cold/warm external caches, misses, negative-cache retries, or coalescing concerns.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed line directly calls a registry implementation that only appends to an in-memory array/Map, and the contribution's create callback returns a no-op disposable.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; retained state is one fixed contribution for a test-only module.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The fixed module-lifetime allocation is bounded and removes two per-render register/dispose cycles rather than introducing scaling work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render an AI customization management editor screenshot fixture
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each render now defines one fixture-local DI instance containing constObservable(options.extensionsSectionBadge). For ordinary fixtures, Extensions is absent from managementSections, so badge resolution never touches this service. In the two Extensions fixtures, editor creation performs one DI lookup and reads the constant observable while building sidebar badge state.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One small service object and constant observable per fixture render; badge work scales with configured management sections, whose fixture lists are fixed at about 8-9 entries, and only one Extensions entry can use the new service.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each fixture owns an isolated instantiation service. Badge evaluation is synchronous and once per active harness derivation; there is no Promise fan-out, queue, limiter, or cross-fixture shared mutable badge state.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The derived badge list resolves observables once per active harness and subsequent reads use the same constant observable. No external cache or repeated miss path is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the transitive call path is defineInstance -> registry getBadge -> accessor.get -> const observable read, all in memory; the contribution is not initializeOnEditorOpen and its widget creation is a no-op.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact number of fixture/theme renders depends on the fixture runner selection, but cost remains constant per render and does not reach an expensive boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added per-render object allocation and DI lookup are bounded test-fixture overhead, while default fixtures do not include the contributed section.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the sole changed file and all diff hunks. Traced registry lifecycle, fixture service creation, editor section construction, badge derivation, and contributed-widget initialization. The change introduces only bounded in-memory test-fixture work and no expensive boundary, hot-path fan-out, unbounded retention, or user-visible performance regression.
